ushers.title: Ushers’ training manual
ushers.intro: Welcome visitors, capture their information once, and pass the care journey to the follow-up team. No staff login is required.
ushers.body:
1. Open the public form

Bookmark Open the public visitor form. You can also find this link on Team Login before signing in. The public form lets you submit information; it does not let you browse the church database.

2. Before capturing a visitor

  1. Explain that the church will use the information for visitor care and follow-up. Confirm the visitor agrees.
  2. Check that another usher has not already entered the same visitor from the same card. Choose one capture method per visitor; do not enter the same card into both the Google Form and this form.
  3. Have the visitor's completed card ready. Only type answers they actually provided. Leave optional unanswered fields blank.

3. Enter the information

  1. Check Service date. It starts with today's Johannesburg date. If capturing an earlier service, change it.
  2. Enter Full name accurately. This is required.
  3. Enter their email and cellphone if provided. Double-check every phone digit; a wrong number prevents follow-up.
  4. Enter the service attended, area, birthday and other supplied answers.
  5. Copy prayer points respectfully. Do not add guesses or personal opinions.
  6. Record the visitor's answer about WhatsApp and membership. Agreement to follow-up does not automatically mean agreement to a WhatsApp group.
  7. Tick the agreement checkbox only after the visitor has agreed.

4. Save and enter the next visitor

  1. Select Submit visitor form once.
  2. Wait while the button says Saving visitor…. Do not close the page.
  3. Look for the success message with the visitor's name and reference.
  4. The visitor fields clear; the service date and service name stay selected for the next entry. Check these before continuing.

If something goes wrong

If there is no success message, do not assume it saved. Keep the form open. If the result is uncertain, ask an admin to check the visitor's name before submitting again. If you entered a wrong number or duplicate, tell the admin the visitor's name and reference; do not submit a second form as a correction.

This form does not save an offline draft. Retain the original visitor card securely until the admin confirms capture, according to church procedure.

End-of-service handover

Tell the admin how many visitor cards were captured and which need checking. Hand urgent prayer or care needs directly to the responsible pastor; submitting the form does not send an emergency alert. Clear the device screen before handing it to someone else.

Practice with the trainer

Explain where the form link is, identify today's service date, and describe the success message. For a live practice submission, first ask the trainer to designate a clearly labelled training record so practice data is not mistaken for a real visitor.

team.title: Follow-up team training manual
team.intro: Work through the people assigned to you, record each contact outcome, and keep the next action clear.
team.body:
Access and help

Open Team Login on your phone or computer. Use your own email and the password supplied by the church administrator. There is no public staff signup. For a forgotten password, ask the administrator to generate another one. Never share an account.

Use Sign out when finished, especially on a shared device. Signing in, approximate location, device information, and activity are recorded. An internet connection is required. If a save fails, keep your work open and read the message before trying again.

Respect each visitor

Use contact information only for authorised church care. Follow the visitor's WhatsApp preference. Keep prayer requests confidential. Notes are shared with authorised leaders and the person assigned to follow up; they are not private personal notes. Record facts and agreed next steps, without unnecessary sensitive details.

1. Start your session

  1. Sign in. Your starting page is the Follow-Up Board.
  2. Open a person's card to see their profile and prayer points.
  3. You can also use People to find someone assigned to you. You cannot see everyone's visitors.
  4. If your list is empty, ask an admin or pastor to assign people to your account.

2. Prepare and contact

Read the existing notes before calling to avoid repeating a conversation. Check the contact details and prayer requests. Open WhatsApp opens the conversation in WhatsApp; it does not send a message automatically. Follow the visitor's preferences and the church's agreed contact times.

3. Record the outcome

  1. Choose the appropriate Follow-up status.
  2. For a return call, set Next follow-up date. Check your device's local time setting.
  3. Enter a short Update summary and select Save follow-up changes. Wait for confirmation.
  4. For a fuller conversation record, use Notes → Add note. Saving a note is separate from saving follow-up changes.
StatusWhen to use it
PendingNo first contact attempt has been recorded.
ContactedYou reached the visitor and had a conversation.
Not reachableYou tried but could not reach the visitor. Add the attempt and next step.
Follow Up AgainAnother conversation is needed. Set a next follow-up date.
CompletedThe agreed follow-up is finished. Add an outcome note.
Voicemail / Not InterestedUse when accurate. Respect a request not to be contacted.

Some older records show Contacted (legacy). Do not change statuses just to improve the dashboard numbers.

A useful note

“Spoke with visitor. They requested a call on Tuesday afternoon about membership. Follow-up arranged for Tuesday 15:00.” Avoid unverified claims and unnecessary personal information. Notes show the author and time.

4. Escalate and finish

Tell the pastor directly when a visitor needs urgent pastoral attention. Notes alone do not notify someone immediately. Ask a leader to correct profile details or change the assigned person. Before signing out, check that each completed call has its status, note and next step saved.

Real-time updates and troubleshooting

Saved changes become visible to authorised leaders and other authorised viewers while connected. If a record is reassigned, you may lose access. If your screen looks stale, check the connection and reload after saving. Do not overwrite another person's work without checking the latest notes.

Practice with the trainer

On a designated training record: open the profile, add a factual note, select Follow Up Again, set a next date, save, then reopen it to verify. Ask the trainer to confirm the change is visible on the leader's screen.

admin.title: Administrator training manual
admin.intro: Manage staff access, distribute visitor care, check activity, and keep the system ready for the team.
admin.body:
Access and help

Open Team Login on your phone or computer. Use your own email and the password supplied by the church administrator. There is no public staff signup. For a forgotten password, ask the administrator to generate another one. Never share an account.

Use Sign out when finished, especially on a shared device. Signing in, approximate location, device information, and activity are recorded. An internet connection is required. If a save fails, keep your work open and read the message before trying again.

Respect each visitor

Use contact information only for authorised church care. Follow the visitor's WhatsApp preference. Keep prayer requests confidential. Notes are shared with authorised leaders and the person assigned to follow up; they are not private personal notes. Record facts and agreed next steps, without unnecessary sensitive details.

1. Create staff access

  1. Open Dashboard → Admin Controls.
  2. Enter the staff member's name and correct email.
  3. Select their role: admin, pastor, or team. Give admin access only to people responsible for system administration.
  4. Select Create user. Wait for confirmation and the generated password.
  5. Give the person their login link, email and generated password privately. Do not place passwords in group chats or training manuals.
  6. Ask them to sign in and confirm their correct starting page.

2. Reset or remove access

In Access Overview, find the correct account and choose Generate password when a reset is needed. The previous password is replaced. Give the new password to that person privately. Use Disable access when someone leaves the role; use Restore access only when authorised. Disabling does not delete their historic notes. The system protects your own access and the last active admin from being disabled through these controls.

3. Receive and assign visitors

  1. After service, compare the ushers' capture count with the new people received.
  2. Open People and select a visitor.
  3. Under Follow-up Management, choose Assigned to, set a next follow-up date if needed, and save.
  4. Repeat until every visitor needing contact has an owner.
  5. Use Correct profile details → Save profile to fix a verified typo. Ask the usher for the original card if uncertain.

The dashboard's “New in the Last 48 Hours” uses capture time. The service date entered by an usher is recorded in Service Feedback. A visitor captured late may therefore appear as new today.

4. Monitor work and logins

Review Awaiting First Contact, Overdue Follow-ups, Prayer Priority, and Follow-Up Snapshot. Open a person's Activity History to inspect recorded views and changes.

Staff Login History shows recorded sign-ins, device/IP and approximate location when supplied, last activity, and estimated active duration. Location is not GPS and may reflect a mobile provider or VPN. A disconnected session is not proof of a deliberate logout. Active duration is an estimate from interaction checks, not a timesheet. Historical sessions before this feature was installed cannot be reconstructed.

System Activity shows recent recorded actions. Browser view logging depends on the client and connection; it is not a guarantee that every view under every failure condition is captured.

5. Reports

  1. Open Reports.
  2. Choose dates, status and assigned user as needed; inspect the preview.
  3. Select Export filtered CSV for a spreadsheet file.
  4. Send to Google Sheets requires the separate reporting integration to be configured. If it reports an error, use CSV and contact the system maintainer.

Date filters refer to capture time. Daily Google Sheets delivery only runs after its integration is configured and enabled. Keep exported files restricted to authorised recipients.

Weekly routine

Review disabled/stale accounts, unassigned visitors, overdue care, possible duplicate entries and failed exports. Check the intake with the ushers. Do not delete records or change database settings casually; request verified corrections from the system maintainer.

Practice with the trainer

Use a designated training account and visitor: create access, assign the visitor, verify the team can see only their assignment, confirm a saved note on your screen, export a filtered CSV, and inspect the recorded login. Do not use real visitor details for demonstrations.

pastors.title: Pastors’ training manual
pastors.intro: See the care needs of the church, oversee follow-up, and support the team with clear next steps.
pastors.body:
Access and help

Open Team Login on your phone or computer. Use your own email and the password supplied by the church administrator. There is no public staff signup. For a forgotten password, ask the administrator to generate another one. Never share an account.

Use Sign out when finished, especially on a shared device. Signing in, approximate location, device information, and activity are recorded. An internet connection is required. If a save fails, keep your work open and read the message before trying again.

Respect each visitor

Use contact information only for authorised church care. Follow the visitor's WhatsApp preference. Keep prayer requests confidential. Notes are shared with authorised leaders and the person assigned to follow up; they are not private personal notes. Record facts and agreed next steps, without unnecessary sensitive details.

1. Review the dashboard

After signing in, start with Prayer Priority, then Awaiting First Contact and Overdue Follow-ups. The new visitor panel covers records captured in the last 48 hours. Open People for the full directory; the dashboard only shows a short list in some panels.

2. Review a person

  1. Open their name to see Full Profile and Prayer Points.
  2. Read the notes and activity history before contacting the visitor.
  3. Record a concise pastoral next step in Notes → Add note. These are shared care notes, not a confidential counselling journal.
  4. If needed, correct verified profile details with Correct profile details.

3. Direct follow-up

Choose an owner under Assigned to, set a status and next follow-up date, enter an update summary, and select Save follow-up changes. The assigned team member can then work on that person. Confirm urgent assignments directly with the team; there is no automatic emergency notification.

StatusWhen to use it
PendingNo first contact attempt has been recorded.
ContactedYou reached the visitor and had a conversation.
Not reachableYou tried but could not reach the visitor. Add the attempt and next step.
Follow Up AgainAnother conversation is needed. Set a next follow-up date.
CompletedThe agreed follow-up is finished. Add an outcome note.
Voicemail / Not InterestedUse when accurate. Respect a request not to be contacted.

Some older records show Contacted (legacy). Do not change statuses just to improve the dashboard numbers.

4. Understand staff oversight

Access Overview lists staff roles and last activity. Staff Login History shows recorded sessions and approximate location/device information. Location is not an exact address; network routing and VPNs can change it. Active time is estimated, and a disconnected session may mean a closed tab or lost connection. Discuss unusual activity with the admin before drawing conclusions.

Staff account creation, generated password resets and access disabling are managed by the administrator in this version. Ask the admin when a team member needs access or a replacement password.

5. Review progress and reports

Use the Follow-Up Board for an overview of statuses, and Reports for date/status/owner filters. Export a filtered CSV when a leadership meeting needs it. Google Sheets export works only when the reporting integration has been configured. Captured At means database entry time; the service date supplied by the usher appears in Service Feedback.

Suggested weekly rhythm

  1. After Sunday service: confirm new visitors arrived and urgent care needs have an owner.
  2. Early in the week: check first contacts and requested return calls.
  3. Before the next service: review outstanding invitations, membership interest and overdue follow-ups.
  4. At the team review: discuss outcomes and obstacles, using notes and statuses together.

Practice with the trainer

Find a designated training visitor, review the prayer request, assign follow-up, add a note, and confirm the team member can see it. Review a filtered report and explain why estimated login duration is not an attendance record.
